title: Steven Tyler civil trial set for May 2027 as judge weighs reopening narrowed claims
excerpt: A Los Angeles judge has set a May 3, 2027 trial date in Julia Misley's civil lawsuit against Aerosmith frontman Steven Tyler, and said he is open to revisiting earlier rulings that narrowed the case.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A Los Angeles judge has set a new trial date in the long-running civil lawsuit against Aerosmith frontman Steven Tyler, scheduling the case for May 3, 2027.

Julia Misley, formerly known as Julia Holcomb, filed the lawsuit in December 2022 under California's Child Victims Act. She alleges that Tyler groomed and sexually abused her over about three years beginning in 1973, when she was 16 years old and he was 25. Tyler disputes her account. The case is a civil lawsuit, not a criminal prosecution, and the allegations have not been proven in court.

Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Lawrence P. Riff set the date at a hearing on Monday, November 9. Billboard reports Riff is the sixth judge to take on the case since 2022.

The case had been set for trial in September 2026, but that date was canceled after the previous judge, Patricia A. Young, recused herself less than two weeks before trial was to begin. In April, Judge Young had ruled that much of Misley's case was barred by the statute of limitations, substantially narrowing the claims to alleged events in California.

Judge Riff told both sides he is open to reconsidering Judge Young's earlier rulings if either side asks, and gave attorneys until November 20 to identify the orders they want reviewed. Misley's attorneys have said they plan to challenge the April ruling that dismissed claims involving alleged events in Massachusetts, Oregon and Washington. Riff expects to hold a hearing on that question in January.

Sources: Billboard; Rolling Stone via NME; Law Commentary.
